Far Cry: Primal team decided in early stages there would be no multiplayer (x-post /v/CoOpGaming)

Personally, I'm pretty happy about that. I'd like the days where a game had to be 2 different things to go away. One of the 2 modes always seems to suffer for it, and people typically tend to play either one or the other anyway. The last multiplayer game I played was DOTA and that was probably at least half a year ago...

I think something as complex as this always depends on the execution. I think a lot of games do just fine with co-op at the core: Diablo 3, Borderlands, Payday 2, Castle Crashers, Monaco, even Rainbow Six: Siege. These are all games where the same content can be played alone or with friends to great effect. The problem is when single-player games try to tack-on co-op modes as a value add; it usually ends up being an afterthought that doesn't draw in people who appreciate good co-op.

Part of me is annoyed when a game company tacks-on co-op as an afterthought (Assassin's Creed Unity, Far Cry) and then interprets the lack of interest to mean no one cares for co-op. People appreciate good co-op and good single-player, and I believe they can exist in the same game but only if they're given equal consideration. I think dropping co-op is a good move for Far Cry because they didn't seem interested in co-op as a core concept, and if they want to focus on single-player exclusively then I think that's sticking more to their core philosophy anyway.

I'm currently following two early access games built with multiplayer support in mind from the beginning, and the amount of work that goes into providing a rock-solid, reliable, seamless multiplayer environment is huge. I agree with /u/ChillyHellion....if a developer is going to do multiplayer, do it from the beginning and do it right o don't do it at all. Deciding up front to not incorporate multiplayer gameplay is better than deciding to add it after the fact because all the forum lobbyists won't shut up about it.

I think that's putting it perfectly. There's nothing wrong with putting in the work early on and building in good multiplayer from the ground up, and there's nothing wrong with putting your resources elsewhere and deciding to focus purely on a robust single-player experience. I just don't care for games that try to tack a game mode on as an easy extra feature, so I can respect Far Cry deciding not to do that with this game.
